unmapped.reason: Collapsed to the icon rail, the row leaves its label span less room than its first character and the ellipsis need, 8px at the large size and none at the others: Chromium draws the first character and the ellipsis clipped at the span, while a Figma text that ends in an ellipsis draws the ellipsis alone. The label hugs its one line instead, and the row clips it at its own edge, where the span ends too, so Figma shows what Chromium draws.

Collapsed to the icon rail at the default and sm sizes, the row's 8px end padding lies between where the label span ends and where the row clips, and the label hugs its one line past the span, so the build cannot show that the row's clip cuts the text off at the span's edge. The span starts at the row's clip edge there, with no room left after the icon and the gap, so neither Chromium nor Figma shows any of the text. At the large size the row has no end padding and clips where the span ends.

#773: a row's shortcut margin reads as the label filling the room before it only where the capture measured the row fitting its layers with a pixel to spare in every mode (`fitsAlongMain`). The popup is as wide as its widest row, which leaves no pixel, and a row whose shortcut the demo leaves out holds no auto margin in the popup's markup to measure, so in those rows the margin stays unmapped.

alike.reason: Base UI marks a read-only stepper `aria-disabled`, not `:disabled`, and no rule reads its `data-readonly`, so it draws as one at rest, its transparent fill showing the read-only field box's muted one. The Number field set's read-only cells show their steppers through this value.
The badge takes `text-sidebar-accent-foreground` both while its menu button is hovered and while the button is active, so the two draw the same.
Each is a range end alone in its week's row, so `rounded-s-full` and `rounded-e-full` round all four corners of both and both fill with `bg-primary`; only which rule rounds which side differs.
An open sub-trigger takes `bg-accent` and `text-accent-foreground` as a highlighted one does, and its chevron inherits the color the highlighted chevron's `**:text-accent-foreground` sets.
`default` is `text-inherit`, which takes the host's color, and the capture's host page sets `--foreground`, the color `foreground` sets. Figma has no parent color for a component to inherit.

An active link sets `font-medium`, as an inactive one does, and `text-foreground`, where an inactive one is `text-inherit` and takes the capture's host color, `--foreground`; neither the Root nor the List sets a color. `aria-current` draws nothing.
